_what: Regions of the PCM design plates that carried a continuous-tone photographic inset (ceramic portrait reproductions of real people). scripts/pcm_photo_mask.py replaces each region with a neutral fill and the Bonney Watson fleur.
_provenance: s15 Track A. Census by eye over contact sheets of all 699 shipped plates (scratch/s15a/sheets); regions confirmed plate by plate at full resolution. Etched/laser portraits and other line art are NOT in scope and are untouched -- only continuous-tone photographic insets are masked. s16 Track C: every one of the 91 regions was re-fit BY HAND to the original inset's true bounds -- director-ordered after the operator saw placeholder ovals larger than the photo they replaced, overlapping engraved words, dates and drawn art. Each region was read off a 4x grid crop of the pre-mask plate (git c670f42) and confirmed against a drawn candidate ellipse, iterating until the box hugged the outer edge of the ceramic rim +~3px and cleared every letter, date, frame line and drawn element outside the inset's own footprint. Where the inset genuinely abuts lettering or drawn art, covering the photograph wins; those are listed in _touchesArt.
_coordinateSpace: pixels in the shipped pcm-design-images/<book>/<num>.webp (700 px long edge), origin top-left, bbox = [x0,y0,x1,y1]
_shapes: oval = ellipse inscribed in the bbox; rect = the bbox itself
_borderline: 2011/1128 NOT MASKED. The whole plate is one continuous-tone laser etching of an infant on black granite -- the etching IS the product, there is no inset to replace, and masking it would leave a black rectangle with a name on it. It is the only continuous-tone image in the entire 2011 book. If the operator wants it gone the right move is to drop the plate, not to mask it.
2020/1006 second image NOT MASKED. Under the name panel is a laser-etched livestock scene, not a photograph of a person. The ceramic portrait on the same plate IS masked.

2020/896 and 2020/952 MASKED. Both are continuous-tone colour photographs (sunset scenes with silhouetted figures) set in an oval inset, so they are the class the ruling names -- but no face is legible in either, so they are the two the operator is most likely to want back.

_director_refit: 2026-08-04: the track's connected-component boxes systematically under-covered (director's 91-region 4x rim sweep found surviving photo crescents on ~a third). Every bbox was re-derived: detector union (chroma + continuous-tone smoothness) anchored on the track box, then two directional-extend passes and two hand-read grid boxes (668, 845), each iteration repainted FROM THE ORIGINAL bytes (git c670f42) so the shipped plate is always a single re-encode. All 91 regions verified clean at 4x by eye in their final state; overgrowth onto engraved text (682 dates, 834 banner, 985 CHAPMAN, 858 dates) was specifically walked back.
_touchesArt: 2020/736 the ceramic rim's top arc runs up to the baseline of "L. BUC..."; the box tops out at y=103, ~5px clear, but there is no room to give.
2020/947 the inset's bottom edge sits on the drawn chevron band; the box follows the rim, so the chevron is clipped where the photograph overlapped it.
2020/891 the rim's right edge stops ~3px short of the "S" of "Sept"; no overlap, but it is the tightest clearance on the sheet.
2020/830 the oval's bottom edge stops 2px above the drawn black bar beneath it.
